item.text:
**6B.4 Research Note**

**Verdict:** mixed, leaning negative. Putin’s 2024 government did fund and expand several social-service programs with real staffing and delivery logic, especially in healthcare and disability/family support. But the broader system still looks patronage-heavy and opaque, with elite loyalty networks, weak accountability, and centralized control dominating the state apparatus.

| Stance | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Support | [Government increased special social payments for medical workers](https://government.ru/news/51150/) | Government of Russia | 2024-03-21 | https://government.ru/news/51150/ | Putin ordered higher monthly social payments for medical workers in rural areas, district centers, and small towns, explicitly to support staffing in primary care. | 6B.4; 6B.2 |
| Support | [Additional financing for rural healthcare workers](https://government.ru/docs/53769/) | Government of Russia | 2024-12-18 | https://government.ru/docs/53769/ | The government extended `Zemsky Doctor` and `Zemsky Paramedic` through 2030, raised compensation, allowed one transfer within the region, and said the program brought about 2,000 specialists in 2024. | 6B.4; 6B.2 |
| Support | [Improving healthcare services for rural areas](https://government.ru/en/news/51246/) | Government of Russia | 2024-03-26 | https://government.ru/en/news/51246/ | The government said medics’ pay supplements were increased again, that personnel shortages were being addressed through `Country Doctor` and `Country Paramedic`, and that these programs would be extended to attract specialists and improve quality. | 6B.4; 6B.2 |
| Support | [State guarantees program for free medical care, 2024-2026](https://government.ru/news/50600/) | Government of Russia | 2024-01-09 | https://government.ru/news/50600/ | Russia kept a universal free-medical-care program in force for 2024-2026, including high-tech and specialized treatment. | 6B.4; 6B.2 |
| Support | [Social Fund operations in the new regions in 2024](https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2024/12/18/276536) | Social Fund of Russia | 2024-12-18 | https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2024/12/18/276536 | The Social Fund reported full-scale benefit administration in occupied/new regions, including pensions, child benefits, disability support, sick-leave digitization, and payments for health workers. | 6B.4; 6B.2; 6B.3 |
| Support | [Rehabilitation support for children with disabilities expanded](https://government.ru/docs/53649/) | Government of Russia | 2024-12-09 | https://government.ru/docs/53649/ | The rehabilitation pilot for children with disabilities expanded from 3 to 38 regions and covered rehab, lodging, meals, and travel costs. | 6B.4; 6B.2; 6B.3 |
| Against | [Russia: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says the system is effectively a kleptocracy: elites receive contracts and protection for loyalty, decision-making is closed, and accountability is weak. That points against merit-based management of social services. | 6B.4 |
| Against | [Russia: Nations in Transit 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024 | Freedom House says the state and its agencies dominate funding for civil society, regional autonomy has been eliminated, and policy space is controlled from above. That is consistent with patronage-based governance rather than professional autonomy. | 6B.4 |
| Against | [Russia: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | The same report says there is little transparency and accountability in day-to-day government, especially at the federal level, where decisions are taken by a small closed circle. | 6B.4 |

**Search gap:** I found strong evidence that the Kremlin funded some social services through technocratic staffing levers, especially in rural healthcare. I did not find strong 2024 evidence that social-service management itself was broadly depoliticized, merit-based, or insulated from patronage networks outside these targeted programs. The best pro evidence is mostly official self-reporting; the best anti evidence is structural governance reporting from Freedom House.
